entries.title: Use causal rolling-origin validation
entries.principle: Model choice must be based on forecasts whose training prefix ends before each validation target.
entries.use_when: Always, especially when selecting among adaptive programs.
entries.avoid_when: Never use random folds or future observations for a forecasting choice.
entries.implementation: Evaluate every candidate on the same ordered cutoffs and aggregate fold errors before seeing the true horizon.

entries.title: Match validation horizon to deployment horizon
entries.principle: One-step accuracy need not rank models correctly for long direct forecasts.
entries.use_when: The requested horizon is a substantial fraction of the history.
entries.avoid_when: Do not select a long-horizon extrapolator using only one-step fit.
entries.implementation: Use the longest feasible rolling holdout, inspect horizon-wise degradation, and shrink unstable extrapolation.

entries.title: Treat residual autocorrelation as unused signal
entries.principle: Strong residual autocorrelation indicates that a model left predictable temporal structure behind.
entries.use_when: Raw history or simple-model errors remain autocorrelated.
entries.avoid_when: A white-noise residual does not prove future regime stability.
entries.implementation: Compare residual lag correlations after fitting level, trend, and seasonal candidates; add AR correction only if holdouts improve.

entries.title: Preserve a repeat-last candidate
entries.principle: A random-walk or locally persistent process makes the final observation a strong hard-to-beat forecast.
entries.use_when: Persistence is high, structure is weak, or alternatives extrapolate aggressively.
entries.avoid_when: Clear recurring seasonality or stable drift survives rolling holdouts.
entries.implementation: Return history[-1] for every step and retain it as a no-op safety candidate.

entries.title: Repeat the last observed season
entries.principle: When a stable seasonal pattern recurs, the value from the same phase of the latest cycle is a strong benchmark.
entries.use_when: At least two cycles are observed and seasonal-lag correlation is material.
entries.avoid_when: Fewer than two cycles, weak seasonal evidence, or a recent regime change.
entries.implementation: Forecast history[len(history)-m+(step mod m)] and compare against nonseasonal candidates.

entries.title: Use global drift as a conservative trend benchmark
entries.principle: The average change from first to last observation projects a random walk with drift without fitting many parameters.
entries.use_when: A long-run trend is visible and local slopes are noisy.
entries.avoid_when: A structural break makes the full-history average obsolete.
entries.implementation: Forecast y_last + h_step*(y_last-y_first)/(n-1), with optional damping selected by holdout.

entries.title: Exponentially smooth an evolving level
entries.principle: Recent observations should receive more weight when a series has a changing level but no durable trend or seasonality.
entries.use_when: Level evolves smoothly and the series is noisy or mean reverting.
entries.avoid_when: Strong trend, seasonality, or an uncorrected level shift dominates.
entries.implementation: Search a small deterministic grid of alpha values on rolling folds; forecast the final smoothed level.

entries.title: Separate level and local trend
entries.principle: A locally linear series can be represented by recursively updated level and slope states.
entries.use_when: Recent slope is stable and rolling folds reward trend continuation.
entries.avoid_when: The horizon is long relative to history or recent slopes conflict.
entries.implementation: Estimate smoothed level and slope; grid-search smoothing constants or approximate with robust local regression.

entries.title: Damp trend extrapolation
entries.principle: Indefinite linear growth is often implausible, so future slope contributions should decay with horizon.
entries.use_when: Trend exists but the horizon is long or slope estimates vary across folds.
entries.avoid_when: A deterministic linear mechanism is strongly supported across several windows.
entries.implementation: Forecast level plus slope times the cumulative powers of phi; select phi below one by rolling validation.

entries.title: Blend smoothed level and drift in a Theta-style forecast
entries.principle: Combining a curvature-suppressed trend line with a locally smoothed component can balance long-run direction and short-run level.
entries.use_when: Nonseasonal or deseasonalized data show trend but local extrapolation is unstable.
entries.avoid_when: Abrupt recent level shifts invalidate the global line.
entries.implementation: Combine a fitted linear drift forecast with a simple-exponential-smoothing forecast; validate the blend weight.

entries.title: Fit recent windows when old regimes are stale
entries.principle: After a persistent structural change, old observations can bias the current level and slope.
entries.use_when: Recent and previous windows have materially different levels or slopes.
entries.avoid_when: The apparent change is a single outlier or normal seasonal phase.
entries.implementation: Compare several suffix lengths under rolling validation and retain a full-history candidate as a safeguard.

entries.title: Estimate level with medians or trimmed means
entries.principle: A few recording spikes should not move the forecasted latent level as much as an ordinary mean.
entries.use_when: The history contains isolated extreme values without persistent follow-through.
entries.avoid_when: Extreme values form a real new regime rather than contamination.
entries.implementation: Compare recent median, trimmed mean, and ordinary level on rolling folds; never silently delete sustained blocks.

entries.title: Use robust slope estimates under spikes
entries.principle: Median pairwise or block slopes resist individual outliers that can dominate least squares.
entries.use_when: A trend is plausible but outliers are detected.
entries.avoid_when: Series is too short for stable slope estimation.
entries.implementation: Estimate slopes across several recent blocks, take a median, and damp it according to horizon.

entries.title: Distinguish a level shift from an isolated outlier
entries.principle: A sustained run at a new level is evidence for a new state; a single spike is not.
entries.use_when: Adjacent recent windows differ in median and the new level persists for several observations.
entries.avoid_when: The shift aligns with an ordinary seasonal phase or immediately reverses.
entries.implementation: Compare pre/post window medians and within-window dispersion; forecast from the post-shift segment only if hindcasts support it.

entries.title: Maintain multiple run-length hypotheses near a changepoint
entries.principle: When the last change location is uncertain, averaging forecasts from plausible suffixes is safer than choosing one cutoff with certainty.
entries.use_when: Recent level or trend changes are large and cutoff choice is unstable.
entries.avoid_when: No change evidence exists or all suffix candidates perform poorly.
entries.implementation: Generate forecasts from multiple recent suffix lengths and weight them by rolling error rather than claiming an exact changepoint.

entries.title: Model stable level autocorrelation
entries.principle: Lagged values can predict a stationary process when autocorrelations persist without trend.
entries.use_when: Lag correlations are material and rolling residuals retain dependence.
entries.avoid_when: Unit-root-like trend makes level autoregression unstable.
entries.implementation: Fit low-order regularized least squares to lagged levels and recursively forecast; keep order small relative to history.

entries.title: Model changes rather than levels for nonstationary histories
entries.principle: Differencing can remove a stochastic trend so autocorrelation in increments can be modelled safely.
entries.use_when: Levels trend strongly while first differences appear more stable.
entries.avoid_when: Differencing amplifies noise or destroys a stable mean-reverting level.
entries.implementation: Fit a small autoregression to first differences, recursively forecast differences, then cumulatively reconstruct levels.

entries.title: Use seasonal differences when level changes but phases recur
entries.principle: Subtracting the value one season ago can expose trend or residual dependence while preserving the seasonal reference.
entries.use_when: Declared seasonal lag is supported and seasonal level evolves.
entries.avoid_when: Too few cycles or unstable seasonal phase.
entries.implementation: Forecast changes relative to lag m, then add them back to recursively available seasonal values.

entries.title: Require empirical evidence before extrapolating seasonality
entries.principle: A declared frequency alone does not guarantee a repeatable seasonal signal.
entries.use_when: A period is supplied but history contains few cycles or weak lag correlation.
entries.avoid_when: Do not force a seasonal profile solely from metadata.
entries.implementation: Compare seasonal-naive against level/trend candidates on identical rolling folds and gate seasonality off when it loses.

entries.title: Estimate a robust phase-of-season profile
entries.principle: A seasonal pattern can be estimated by pooling corresponding phases across cycles while resisting abnormal cycles.
entries.use_when: Several cycles exist and seasonal-lag correlation is stable.
entries.avoid_when: Only one cycle exists or seasonality changes rapidly.
entries.implementation: Center each recent cycle, take a median by phase, and add it to a separately forecast level or trend.

entries.title: Forecast additive seasonal and adjusted components separately
entries.principle: When seasonal amplitude is roughly independent of level, additive decomposition isolates a reusable seasonal profile.
entries.use_when: Seasonality is supported and variance is roughly stable across levels.
entries.avoid_when: Seasonal amplitude scales with level or too few cycles are observed.
entries.implementation: Subtract a phase profile, forecast the adjusted series with level/trend logic, then restore the profile.

entries.title: Use log or ratio seasonality when amplitude scales with level
entries.principle: Multiplicative effects become additive on a log scale and preserve proportional seasonal changes.
entries.use_when: Values are strictly positive and variability or seasonal amplitude increases with level.
entries.avoid_when: Zeros or negative values occur, or back-transformation bias is uncontrolled.
entries.implementation: Model log values or phase ratios, back-transform, and compare against untransformed candidates on original-scale holdouts.

entries.title: Represent smooth cycles with Fourier terms
entries.principle: Sine/cosine bases compactly represent smooth periodic patterns and can coexist with trend.
entries.use_when: Cycles are smooth, repeated, and supported by several periods.
entries.avoid_when: Sharp phase-specific effects, shifting period, or fewer than two cycles.
entries.implementation: Fit a small number of harmonics plus intercept/trend by least squares; select harmonic count by rolling validation.

entries.title: Allow more than one independently supported cycle
entries.principle: Sub-daily, daily, and weekly data can contain nested periodicities that one seasonal lag cannot represent.
entries.use_when: Distinct ACF or spectral peaks survive holdouts and sufficient cycles exist for each.
entries.avoid_when: Do not infer long cycles from less than two repeats.
entries.implementation: Combine small Fourier bases or repeated profiles for only the validated lags; penalize excessive harmonics.

entries.title: Stabilize level-dependent variance
entries.principle: Log or power transforms can make proportional errors and changing variance easier to model.
entries.use_when: Dispersion grows with level and values permit a valid transform.
entries.avoid_when: Zeros/negatives invalidate log, or original-scale loss makes back-transform bias dominant.
entries.implementation: Compare identity, log1p for nonnegative data, and square-root transforms; score after inverse transformation.

entries.title: Separate nonzero size from arrival interval
entries.principle: For intermittent nonnegative demand, ordinary smoothing confounds event size with long zero gaps; SBA corrects bias in Croston-style estimates.
entries.use_when: Many observations are zero and positive events occur irregularly.
entries.avoid_when: Zeros are missing-data codes or the target can be negative.
entries.implementation: Smooth positive sizes and inter-arrival intervals separately, apply the SBA bias factor, and compare with zero/repeat-last baselines.

entries.title: Model event probability and positive magnitude separately
entries.principle: An intermittent series has two mechanisms: whether an event occurs and how large it is.
entries.use_when: Zero frequency is high but event rate or size changes over time.
entries.avoid_when: Zeros are ordinary continuous values rather than absence events.
entries.implementation: Estimate recent event probability and robust positive size, optionally by seasonal phase, then multiply for an expected point forecast.

entries.title: Respect known support without hiding model failure
entries.principle: Counts, demand, occupancy, and physical intensities often cannot be negative.
entries.use_when: All historical values and target semantics support a nonnegative domain.
entries.avoid_when: A differenced, anomaly, or balance series can legitimately be negative.
entries.implementation: Prefer positive-scale models; clipping is only a final candidate and must be validated because it can mask bad extrapolation.

entries.title: Test a bounded-range forecast for percentage-like histories
entries.principle: A history confined to 0--100 may encode a percentage or capacity rate with hard bounds.
entries.use_when: Metadata and observed scale jointly indicate a rate or occupancy percentage.
entries.avoid_when: Numeric range alone is not proof of a hard bound.
entries.implementation: Generate both unconstrained and [0,100]-bounded candidates; let rolling validation and target semantics decide.

entries.title: Reduce complexity for short histories
entries.principle: Short series cannot reliably estimate many lags, harmonics, changepoints, or validation folds.
entries.use_when: History contains fewer than roughly three seasonal cycles or fewer than 64 points.
entries.avoid_when: Do not interpret in-sample fit as evidence for a high-dimensional model.
entries.implementation: Favor level, damped trend, seasonal naive, and small ensembles; cap lag/harmonic counts aggressively.

entries.title: Shrink unstable structure over long horizons
entries.principle: Slope, autoregressive recursion, and fine seasonal detail compound estimation error far beyond the observed history.
entries.use_when: Forecast horizon approaches or exceeds half the history length.
entries.avoid_when: A known deterministic mechanism fixes the future path.
entries.implementation: Damp trend, decay AR effects toward a level, and blend with conservative baselines using horizon-matched validation.

entries.title: Average genuinely different validated forecasts
entries.principle: Combining models can reduce method-specific error; simple averages are often difficult to beat.
entries.use_when: Several candidates have comparable rolling error and make nonidentical forecasts.
entries.avoid_when: Do not average many clones or include catastrophically unstable candidates.
entries.implementation: Blend two or three structurally diverse candidates equally or by conservative validation weights.

entries.title: Convert historical evidence into conservative model weights
entries.principle: Relative rolling errors provide evidence for ranking hypotheses, but small score differences are uncertain.
entries.use_when: Multiple candidates are valid and no one method dominates every fold.
entries.avoid_when: Near-zero training error or one anomalous fold should not create an extreme weight.
entries.implementation: Use softened inverse-error or rank weights, cap any single weight, and preserve the equal-weight alternative.

entries.title: Express evolving level and trend as latent states
entries.principle: State-space models distinguish noisy observations from an evolving latent process and update states recursively.
entries.use_when: Level/trend changes gradually, observations are noisy, or some history is unreliable.
entries.avoid_when: A simple deterministic seasonal pattern already wins decisively.
entries.implementation: Approximate local-level/local-linear-trend filtering with deterministic exponential updates; vary process-to-observation responsiveness across candidates.

entries.title: Maintain component-level hypotheses
entries.principle: Trend, seasonality, cycles, regression effects, and noise can be represented as separate uncertain components.
entries.use_when: Several mechanisms plausibly coexist and incomplete information prevents one certain model.
entries.avoid_when: Do not claim Bayesian probabilities without a likelihood or empirical calibration.
entries.implementation: Generate explicit component combinations, state assumptions, and use rolling evidence as an approximate posterior ranking.

entries.title: View covariance kernels as compositional hypotheses
entries.principle: Constant, smooth trend, periodic, and noise kernels encode different beliefs about function similarity and can be added or multiplied.
entries.use_when: The history is smooth or periodic and uncertainty over functional form matters.
entries.avoid_when: Full GP fitting is too costly or the series has abrupt unmodelled breaks.
entries.implementation: Use kernel ideas to motivate smooth local regression, periodic bases, and additive components; validate executable approximations rather than inventing uncalibrated certainty.

entries.title: Let uncertainty grow with forecast distance
entries.principle: Multi-step forecasts accumulate innovation and parameter uncertainty, especially under recursive dynamics.
entries.use_when: Horizon is long or candidate forecasts diverge.
entries.avoid_when: A point-only evaluation does not justify pretending uncertainty is zero.
entries.implementation: Use candidate dispersion and fold variation as uncertainty signals; lower confidence when extrapolations diverge.

entries.title: Use a robust mean for weak stationary structure
entries.principle: When serial dependence and trend are weak, estimating a stable central level can beat extrapolation.
entries.use_when: Lag-one correlation and trend effect are both small.
entries.avoid_when: Persistent level, trend, seasonality, or a recent shift is present.
entries.implementation: Compare full-history mean, trimmed mean, and recent mean with repeat-last using rolling folds.

entries.title: Check cycle phase stability before extrapolation
entries.principle: A high correlation at one lag may arise from trend or a transient oscillation rather than a stable phase-locked cycle.
entries.use_when: An empirical lag peak exists without a trusted seasonal period.
entries.avoid_when: Do not extrapolate a detected period unless multiple nonoverlapping cycles align.
entries.implementation: Compare phase profiles across early and recent cycles and require rolling improvement over trend/level baselines.

entries.title: Retrieve historical states and directly reuse their continuations
entries.principle: If the recent delay-coordinate state closely matches an earlier state, the observed path following that earlier state is a data-driven multi-step hypothesis that need not recurse through a fitted equation.
entries.use_when: The history is long enough to contain candidate windows with complete horizon-length continuations, including nonlinear or recurring regimes.
entries.avoid_when: No eligible historical match has a complete continuation, the current state is novel, or close matches imply mutually incompatible futures.
entries.implementation: Search several context lengths; exclude any match whose continuation overlaps the current query; normalize level and optionally scale; rank on recent shape or changes; map the best complete continuation back to the current level/scale; compare directly on rolling holdouts.

entries.title: Match shape independently of absolute level and amplitude
entries.principle: Z-normalized levels or standardized first differences can recognize repeated dynamics that occur at different baselines or scales.
entries.use_when: Similar rises, falls, cycles, or recoveries recur at different absolute levels.
entries.avoid_when: Absolute level itself determines the dynamics, normalization is unstable for near-constant windows, or the nearest distances are all large.
entries.implementation: For multiple window lengths, compare centered/scaled levels and first differences; retrieve several nonoverlapping neighbors with complete continuations; restore current offset/robust scale and average only compatible paths.

entries.title: Abstain when historical analogues are weak or disagree
entries.principle: Nearest-neighbor prediction is conditional on recurrence; a nearest point always exists numerically even when it is not meaningfully close.
entries.use_when: An analogue forecast is considered alongside level, trend, seasonal, or TSFM candidates.
entries.avoid_when: Never force an analogue solely because it is the closest available window.
entries.implementation: Require complete causal continuations, compare distance against typical within-history neighbor distances, measure continuation dispersion, and fall back or blend conservatively when similarity is weak.

entries.title: Select analogue representation and window length causally
entries.principle: Short windows find local motifs but create false matches; long windows identify regimes but leave few eligible continuations.
entries.use_when: History permits several context lengths and the deployment horizon is multi-step.
entries.avoid_when: Do not tune context length on the unknown target horizon.
entries.implementation: Evaluate a small deterministic grid of context lengths, level-vs-difference normalization, neighbor counts, and direct continuations at rolling origins; prefer stable settings across folds or average near-ties.

entries.title: Treat a pretrained TSFM as one transferable prior
entries.principle: Pretraining across diverse real and synthetic series can yield useful zero-shot forecasts for unseen histories.
entries.use_when: A fixed TSFM backbone is available and its historical hindcasts are valid.
entries.avoid_when: Do not assume pretraining coverage or superiority on a specific regime.
entries.implementation: Execute the fixed TSFM unchanged, score it on the same rolling folds, and expose it as a candidate rather than an oracle.

entries.title: Keep transparent statistical complements to a TSFM
entries.principle: A global pretrained model and local statistical rules have different failure modes, so either may win on a particular series.
entries.use_when: Running the combined Setting 2 variant.
entries.avoid_when: Do not imitate neural weights in generated code or select by reputation.
entries.implementation: Compare the fixed TSFM with seasonal-naive, damped trend, robust regime, and validated ensemble candidates under equal cutoffs.

entries.title: Validate TSFM behavior at the requested horizon
entries.principle: Zero-shot benchmark strength does not guarantee stable recursive or out-of-training-range long-horizon behavior.
entries.use_when: A TSFM candidate forecasts a horizon large relative to observed context.
entries.avoid_when: Do not select from short hindcasts alone.
entries.implementation: Use horizon-matched folds where feasible and preserve conservative statistical candidates when the TSFM degrades with distance.

entries.title: Scale errors against an in-sample naive forecast
entries.principle: Raw errors are not comparable across series scales; MASE normalizes by a causal naive error scale.
entries.use_when: Candidate stability must be compared across folds with different levels or across multiple series.
entries.avoid_when: The naive scaling denominator is zero or nearly zero.
entries.implementation: Compute the mean absolute one-step naive or seasonal-naive error on each training prefix; use a guarded denominator and retain raw MAE beside the scaled score.

entries.title: Inspect error by forecast distance
entries.principle: An acceptable average can hide rapidly increasing error at the far end of a multi-step horizon.
entries.use_when: The requested horizon spans many steps or at least one seasonal cycle.
entries.avoid_when: Do not choose a model from a single favorable step.
entries.implementation: Aggregate absolute or symmetric percentage error separately for early, middle, and late horizon blocks; reject candidates whose tail error is unstable.

entries.title: Prefer stable fold performance over one lucky origin
entries.principle: Model-selection variance is high when a candidate wins through one anomalous validation cutoff.
entries.use_when: Several rolling origins are available and candidate rankings vary.
entries.avoid_when: Do not discard a real recent regime solely because older folds differ; compare recent-weighted and equal-weight views.
entries.implementation: Track median fold loss, worst-fold loss, and win count; break close mean-score ties using lower dispersion and fewer catastrophic folds.

entries.title: Compare forecasts on paired origins
entries.principle: Loss differences on the same origins isolate model effects better than comparing unrelated aggregate errors.
entries.use_when: Two candidates are close and enough common hindcast origins exist.
entries.avoid_when: Formal asymptotic significance claims are unreliable with very few or strongly overlapping origins.
entries.implementation: Compute per-origin loss differences, win fraction, and a simple paired bootstrap; preserve the incumbent when the interval spans a material regression.

entries.title: Search a small error-trend-seasonality component grid
entries.principle: Exponential-smoothing forecasts arise from combinations of level, trend, damping, and seasonal states rather than one universal smoother.
entries.use_when: The series has a plausible evolving level, trend, or supported seasonal component.
entries.avoid_when: Do not fit a highly parameterized component combination to a short history.
entries.implementation: Construct a bounded grid over level-only, additive trend, damped trend, and additive seasonal updates; select only with identical rolling origins.

entries.title: Tune damping from long-horizon stability
entries.principle: A damping parameter trades short-run trend continuation against implausible long-run extrapolation.
entries.use_when: A trend is visible but its magnitude changes across suffixes or validation origins.
entries.avoid_when: Do not choose damping from in-sample fit alone.
entries.implementation: Evaluate a small grid such as phi in {0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.98, 1.0}; score at the deployment horizon and retain phi=1 only when consistently superior.

entries.title: Difference persistent nonstationary levels before AR fitting
entries.principle: Autoregression on an integrated level can create spurious mean reversion or explosive long forecasts; first differences may be closer to stationary.
entries.use_when: Level persistence is very high and differenced values have weak serial correlation.
entries.avoid_when: Over-differencing a stationary or strongly mean-reverting series adds noise and negative autocorrelation.
entries.implementation: Compare level AR, first-difference AR, drift, and repeat-last on the same folds; integrate differenced forecasts exactly once.

entries.title: Use a parsimonious AR order search
entries.principle: Information-criterion-guided ARIMA search favors adequate residual structure without unrestricted lag growth.
entries.use_when: Autocorrelation remains after removing level, trend, or seasonality and history is sufficient.
entries.avoid_when: Short histories and regime shifts make high-order coefficients unstable.
entries.implementation: Fit only small AR orders with least squares or ridge regularization, compare differencing choices, and let rolling forecast error override in-sample fit.

entries.title: Seasonally difference only when phase recurrence is stable
entries.principle: Seasonal differencing removes repeating phase levels but amplifies noise when the seasonal relation is weak.
entries.use_when: Several cycles are observed and seasonal-lag correlation persists across windows.
entries.avoid_when: Weak seasonal evidence, fewer than two full cycles, or a recent phase change.
entries.implementation: Compare y[t]-y[t-m] modeling against seasonal naive and direct seasonal profiles; integrate using the last observed cycle.

entries.title: Add a small AR correction to structured baselines
entries.principle: Trend or seasonal models may capture the mean structure while leaving short-memory residual dependence.
entries.use_when: A transparent baseline is good but its causal residuals remain autocorrelated.
entries.avoid_when: Residual correlation is caused by a missed regime break or changes sign across folds.
entries.implementation: Generate base hindcast residuals, fit a low-order regularized AR model to residuals only, recursively add corrections, and keep the uncorrected base candidate.

entries.title: Forecast horizon blocks directly when recursion compounds error
entries.principle: Direct multi-output strategies avoid feeding uncertain predictions back as if observed.
entries.use_when: The horizon is long and recursive candidates drift or oscillate unrealistically.
entries.avoid_when: History is too short to estimate separate horizon effects.
entries.implementation: Estimate separate early, middle, and late horizon offsets or regressions from rolling examples; concatenate smooth blocks and compare with recursive forecasts.

entries.title: Reject unstable recursive trajectories
entries.principle: Iterating a one-step model compounds coefficient and state errors over the horizon.
entries.use_when: AR, local-linear, or nonlinear rules feed forecasts back recursively.
entries.avoid_when: Do not judge recursion only by one-step residual error.
entries.implementation: Run horizon-matched hindcasts; reject paths that explode, collapse, alternate unnaturally, or leave the historical scale without repeated validation support.

entries.title: Combine direct and recursive multi-step hypotheses
entries.principle: Direct and recursive strategies have different bias and variance profiles, so neither dominates universally.
entries.use_when: Both strategies pass causal validation and disagree mainly at distant horizons.
entries.avoid_when: Do not blend a recursively unstable trajectory.
entries.implementation: Blend validated direct-block and recursive candidates with horizon-dependent weights that shift toward the more stable tail forecast.

entries.title: Decompose multiple recurring seasonal periods
entries.principle: High-frequency series can contain several seasonal patterns that a single seasonal index cannot represent.
entries.use_when: More than one stable empirical lag is present and enough cycles of each period are observed.
entries.avoid_when: Do not infer multiple seasons from harmonics of one peak or from fewer than two recurrences.
entries.implementation: Sequentially estimate robust phase means for the longest supported period and then shorter periods; forecast the residual level/trend and add components back.

entries.title: Use robust seasonal decomposition under isolated spikes
entries.principle: Robust STL downweights unusual remainder values so they do not distort trend and seasonal components.
entries.use_when: Supported seasonality coexists with isolated outliers.
entries.avoid_when: A sustained change should be modeled as a regime, not downweighted as noise.
entries.implementation: Approximate robust decomposition with phase medians, a moving-median trend, and residual clipping; validate against the unmodified seasonal profile.

entries.title: Weight recent cycles when phase levels evolve
entries.principle: Seasonal shape may persist while its baseline or phase-specific levels change gradually.
entries.use_when: Recent cycles correlate with older cycles but have a shifted level or changing phase amplitude.
entries.avoid_when: A one-off partial cycle should not erase longer stable evidence.
entries.implementation: Compute phase profiles for several recent-cycle counts, align their levels, and select the recency weight with rolling origins.

entries.title: Allow seasonal amplitude to track the local level
entries.principle: Multiplicative seasonality is plausible when seasonal variation grows with the series level.
entries.use_when: Cycle amplitude and local level rise or fall together on a nonnegative series.
entries.avoid_when: Zeros, negative values, or stable absolute amplitude make multiplicative scaling unsafe.
entries.implementation: Compare additive phase offsets with phase ratios on a guarded positive scale; cap ratios and reverse the transform after forecasting.

entries.title: Compare forecasts from explicitly segmented regimes
entries.principle: Penalized changepoint detection separates persistent distributional changes from gradual noise.
entries.use_when: Several level or variance shifts appear in a sufficiently long history.
entries.avoid_when: Short series or regular seasonality can create false segment boundaries.
entries.implementation: Use a deterministic dynamic-programming or bounded binary segmentation over robust mean costs; forecast from the last segment and retain full-history alternatives.

entries.title: Treat changepoint penalty as model uncertainty
entries.principle: One penalty can under-segment or over-segment, especially near the forecast origin.
entries.use_when: Plausible last-segment starts vary across reasonable penalties.
entries.avoid_when: Do not average segments that fail horizon-matched validation.
entries.implementation: Evaluate a small penalty grid, build last-segment level/trend candidates, and combine only near-tied settings with compatible forecasts.

entries.title: Mix recent-regime and long-history forecasts
entries.principle: A detected break may be persistent, temporary, or spurious; maintaining both regime assumptions avoids an irreversible choice.
entries.use_when: A recent shift is material but only a short post-change segment is observed.
entries.avoid_when: Do not give old regimes large weight after repeated post-change validation confirms persistence.
entries.implementation: Create last-segment, full-history, and shrinkage-blend forecasts; choose weight by analogous historical cutoffs or conservative validation.

entries.title: Update occurrence probability during zero runs
entries.principle: TSB updates demand occurrence probability every period, allowing forecasts to decay during obsolescence-like zero runs.
entries.use_when: Nonnegative demand is intermittent and the latest zero run may indicate declining occurrence probability.
entries.avoid_when: Structural calendar zeros or censoring should not be interpreted as obsolescence.
entries.implementation: Exponentially smooth nonzero size only on arrivals and Bernoulli occurrence every step; multiply the two states and tune smoothing causally.

entries.title: Distinguish ordinary gaps from an unusually long terminal zero run
entries.principle: The age since the last nonzero event is informative relative to the empirical distribution of inter-arrival gaps.
entries.use_when: Zeros dominate and the series ends with a run of zeros.
entries.avoid_when: Do not force a zero forecast when terminal age is typical for the process.
entries.implementation: Compare terminal zero-run length with historical gap quantiles; retain SBA for ordinary gaps and add TSB or zero candidates only for unusually long runs.

entries.title: Aggregate sparse demand before modeling its level
entries.principle: Temporal aggregation can reduce zero inflation and expose a smoother demand-rate signal.
entries.use_when: Events are very sparse but the forecast horizon spans many base periods.
entries.avoid_when: Aggregation that exceeds the horizon destroys timing information.
entries.implementation: Sum over a small grid of block sizes, forecast block totals with level methods, disaggregate uniformly or by validated within-block profiles, and compare at native resolution.

entries.title: Validate a small Box-Cox transformation grid
entries.principle: Power transformations can stabilize variance and make additive dynamics appropriate on the transformed scale.
entries.use_when: A positive series has level-dependent variance or a wide dynamic range.
entries.avoid_when: Nonpositive values require a justified offset, and transformed-scale fit alone is insufficient.
entries.implementation: Compare identity, square-root, and log transforms with a documented positive offset; invert every forecast and score on the original scale.

entries.title: Distinguish median and mean after inverse log transformation
entries.principle: Exponentiating a log-scale point forecast targets a conditional median, not generally the original-scale mean.
entries.use_when: Log or log1p modeling materially improves positive heteroscedastic data.
entries.avoid_when: Do not apply a large bias correction from a few unstable residuals.
entries.implementation: Generate both direct inverse and guarded residual-variance-corrected inverses; select on original-scale rolling MAE or the deployment loss.

entries.title: Separate stochastic differencing from deterministic detrending
entries.principle: A random-walk-like level and a deterministic trend require different transformations and reintegration assumptions.
entries.use_when: The raw level is nonstationary but both drift and integrated-process explanations are plausible.
entries.avoid_when: Do not difference twice without strong residual evidence.
entries.implementation: Compare first-difference modeling, robust linear detrending plus residual modeling, and undifferenced damped trend under identical long-horizon folds.

entries.title: Trim catastrophic candidates before averaging
entries.principle: A robust ensemble gains diversity without allowing one explosive trajectory to dominate its mean.
entries.use_when: Several validated candidates are available and occasional programs extrapolate far outside the group.
entries.avoid_when: Do not trim a lone but consistently validated regime specialist merely because it differs.
entries.implementation: At each horizon take the median or a trimmed mean of candidates that pass fold and finite-value gates; preserve the best single candidate for comparison.

entries.title: Use forecast disagreement as an abstention signal
entries.principle: Wide dispersion among credible model families indicates structural uncertainty not captured by one hindcast score.
entries.use_when: Top candidates have similar validation loss but materially different future paths.
entries.avoid_when: Duplicate implementations should not create false consensus.
entries.implementation: Measure scale-normalized median absolute deviation across structurally distinct forecasts; lower revision confidence and shrink toward robust consensus when disagreement is high.

entries.title: Let ensemble weights vary with forecast distance
entries.principle: A local autoregression may dominate near-term while damped trend, seasonality, or direct methods are safer later.
entries.use_when: Horizon-wise validation rankings change consistently from early to late steps.
entries.avoid_when: Too few folds make step-specific weights noisy.
entries.implementation: Estimate weights for two or three coarse horizon blocks, shrink each toward equal weights, and smooth boundaries between blocks.

entries.title: Bag decomposition-based forecasts with block residuals
entries.principle: Resampling decomposed remainders explores data and model uncertainty while preserving trend and seasonality.
entries.use_when: A long seasonal history has autocorrelated residuals and several close component models.
entries.avoid_when: Short histories, abrupt unresolved regimes, or independent residual shuffling that destroys temporal structure.
entries.implementation: Decompose into robust trend, seasonal profile, and remainder; moving-block-resample the remainder, refit simple component models, and average forecasts.

entries.title: Use out-of-fold residuals for empirical uncertainty
entries.principle: In-sample residuals understate forecast error; causal hindcast residuals reflect model and horizon effects.
entries.use_when: Multiple rolling origins provide residuals at relevant forecast distances.
entries.avoid_when: Do not pool residuals across incompatible regimes without recency checks.
entries.implementation: Store signed residuals by coarse horizon block, add empirical quantiles to the point path, and report sample count and coverage diagnostics.

entries.title: Preserve temporal dependence in residual trajectories
entries.principle: Independent residual draws destroy serial correlation and underrepresent persistent forecast errors.
entries.use_when: Residuals are autocorrelated and probabilistic trajectories are required.
entries.avoid_when: Very few residual blocks or unresolved nonstationarity make empirical paths unreliable.
entries.implementation: Sample contiguous residual blocks, add them to the deterministic path, enforce physical constraints after sampling, and retain the unperturbed path.

entries.title: Use sequential conformal residual updates for time series
entries.principle: EnbPI adapts conformal prediction to dependent dynamic time series through ensemble leave-one-out residuals and sequential updates.
entries.use_when: Resolved outcomes arrive sequentially and an ensemble forecaster is available.
entries.avoid_when: Do not claim exact exchangeable conformal coverage under arbitrary distribution shift.
entries.implementation: Maintain only resolved, chronological residuals; form empirical residual quantiles around ensemble forecasts and update after each outcome, never from unresolved test labels.

entries.title: Scale interval width with predicted difficulty
entries.principle: Conformalized quantile regression adapts interval width to heteroscedastic inputs while calibrating residual nonconformity.
entries.use_when: Forecast error scale changes with level, regime, or horizon.
entries.avoid_when: A tiny calibration set cannot support fine conditional adjustment.
entries.implementation: Estimate a base width from analogous fold residuals, scale it by local volatility or candidate dispersion, and calibrate the final multiplier on held-out origins.

entries.title: Select probabilistic forecasts with proper scores
entries.principle: Proper scoring rules reward calibrated distributions without encouraging strategic over- or under-dispersion.
entries.use_when: Candidate quantiles or trajectories are available rather than only points.
entries.avoid_when: MAE alone cannot establish probability calibration.
entries.implementation: Use CRPS or averaged pinball loss on rolling origins; report empirical coverage and width separately so sharp but undercovered intervals are visible.

entries.title: Use residual stacks of trend and seasonal bases as hypotheses
entries.principle: N-BEATS shows that backward residual refinement and forward basis expansion can separate interpretable trend and seasonality.
entries.use_when: A TSFM or neural candidate is available and transparent basis candidates are needed as complements.
entries.avoid_when: Do not claim to reproduce trained N-BEATS with an unfitted polynomial.
entries.implementation: Generate low-degree trend and harmonic forward bases, subtract each fitted backcast sequentially, and validate the resulting additive forecast as a lightweight structural analogue.

entries.title: Represent long horizons at multiple temporal resolutions
entries.principle: N-HiTS uses hierarchical interpolation and multi-rate sampling to model long-horizon components efficiently.
entries.use_when: The horizon is long and the series contains both slow and fast variation.
entries.avoid_when: Coarse aggregation can erase narrow spikes or event effects.
entries.implementation: Build native-resolution, block-mean, and smooth low-rate forecasts; interpolate coarse paths back to the horizon and combine only after horizon-matched validation.

entries.title: Normalize local scale before borrowing a global prior
entries.principle: DeepAR normalizes series scale and learns a conditional probabilistic autoregressive model across related series.
entries.use_when: A global or pretrained model is combined with local rules across widely varying magnitudes.
entries.avoid_when: A local structural break may not be represented by global scaling alone.
entries.implementation: Normalize by a robust local magnitude for comparison and candidate generation, then restore scale; always validate the global candidate locally.

entries.title: Separate known-future from observed-only covariates
entries.principle: Multi-horizon models distinguish static, known-future, and historically observed inputs because their availability differs at forecast time.
entries.use_when: Context documents imply calendar or scheduled future drivers and a contextual model is considered.
entries.avoid_when: Do not feed realized future measurements or retrospective summaries as if known at the cutoff.
entries.implementation: Tag every external feature with availability time; expose only static and cutoff-known future values, and keep observed-only variables lagged behind the origin.

entries.title: Combine local exponential states with a global nonlinear prior
entries.principle: ES-RNN demonstrates that local level and seasonality normalization can complement a globally learned recurrent model.
entries.use_when: A global TSFM is available but local scale or seasonal states are strong.
entries.avoid_when: Do not replace local validation with global benchmark reputation.
entries.implementation: Compare the fixed global forecast with locally normalized seasonal and exponential-smoothing candidates; blend only when their errors are complementary across folds.

entries.title: Reconcile forecasts across temporal aggregation levels
entries.principle: Forecasts made at native, weekly, or other aggregate levels encode different signal-to-noise tradeoffs and should agree after aggregation.
entries.use_when: The horizon contains complete aggregation blocks and native-resolution data are noisy.
entries.avoid_when: Partial terminal blocks or event-driven spikes can make uniform disaggregation misleading.
entries.implementation: Create native and block-aggregate forecasts, disaggregate coarse totals using recent validated profiles, and adjust them so block sums match before scoring.

entries.title: Use aggregation agreement as a stability check
entries.principle: A forecast that changes radically under modest temporal aggregation may be fitting high-frequency noise.
entries.use_when: Native observations are volatile but slower level or seasonal structure is plausible.
entries.avoid_when: Known short-lived events legitimately create high-frequency departures.
entries.implementation: Forecast at two small aggregation factors, map both paths to native resolution, and penalize candidates whose aggregate totals disagree without historical support.

entries.title: Model bounded series on a bounded link scale
entries.principle: Direct linear extrapolation can violate known percentage or proportion bounds.
entries.use_when: The complete history and target semantics support a fixed lower and upper bound.
entries.avoid_when: Observed historical range alone is not proof of a physical bound.
entries.implementation: When bounds are known, compare clipping with a guarded logit-style transform; invert to the original range and validate near-bound behavior.

entries.title: Keep count forecasts nonnegative without forced rounding
entries.principle: A point forecast for a count is an expected value and may validly be fractional even though observations are integers.
entries.use_when: The series is nonnegative and integer-valued.
entries.avoid_when: Rounding each horizon step can add avoidable bias; negative expectations are invalid.
entries.implementation: Model level, occurrence, or transformed counts continuously, clip only below zero, and round only if the downstream contract explicitly requires integer actions.
